assessment.nobel_worthiness: Systematic theoretical and empirical analysis of how constitutions, electoral rules and political institutions shape fiscal policy, state capacity and economic outcomes. It opened political economics as a field with broad reach into public finance, macro and development.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central, long-running coauthors of the field-defining synthesis and the empirical work on electoral rules and constitutions. Besley is a major contributor on state capacity and accountability but is left out here to keep the proposal to two.
assessment.maturity: Work dates from the 1990s and has been confirmed, extended and widely taught for decades. The 2024 institutions prize covered adjacent but distinct ground, so the field is established without being redundant.
uncertainties: Persson is at the IIES, as is the chair, a disclosed connection that this simulation does not adjudicate.
Whether the committee prefers to include Besley in place of one of the two named is open.
Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize may be judged significant.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-constraint model of credit cycles shows how small shocks are amplified and persist through asset prices and borrowing limits. It is now a standard building block of macro-finance and financial-crisis analysis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore's 1997 paper is the clear origin of the mechanism. Gertler and Gilchrist are important on the financial accelerator and its empirics, but the core idea is credited most cleanly to the two.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of use, including in post-2008 policy models, make the confirmation record strong. The 2022 banking and crisis prize touched related themes but not this mechanism.
uncertainties: Relative credit between Kiyotaki–Moore and the Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist accelerator strand is debatable, and Bernanke already holds a prize.
Possible overlap with the 2022 prize could weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Staggered nominal rigidities, interest-rate rules and the micro-founded New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary-policy analysis and central-bank practice. Impact on both academic and policy practice is very large.
assessment.attribution: Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule) and Woodford (the integrated framework) form a defensible trio. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets are also substantial, so the cut is contestable and some credit will be left out.
assessment.maturity: The core ideas are from the 1980s to 2000s and have been confirmed by decades of use in practice. Maturity is not a concern.
uncertainties: The list is broad and attribution is diffuse across many contributors.
Whether a prize for the framework is better split between theory and applied-policy contributions is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a tractable, measurable account of why cross-country income and productivity differ, linking micro-level distortions to aggregate TFP. It is highly influential in growth, development and macro.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow's 2009 paper is the key contribution. Restuccia and Rogerson's related work is a close parallel, and Rogerson is not on the list, which complicates exclusive credit.
assessment.maturity: Seventeen years of heavy use and replication, along with debate on measurement, indicate a maturing but still evolving literature.
uncertainties: Sensitivity of the measured gains to measurement error and model assumptions is disputed.
Credit overlap with Restuccia and Rogerson may weaken a pure Hsieh–Klenow attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law and finance linked legal origins and investor protection to financial development and ownership structure, opening a major empirical research program in comparative institutions and corporate finance.
assessment.attribution: The core legal-origins papers are by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. A three-person cap forces the exclusion of Vishny, who is a co-author on the foundational work.
assessment.maturity: The program is 25-30 years old and well cited, though the legal-origins hypothesis has been contested on identification and robustness.
uncertainties: The legal-origins thesis has been critiqued, and the empirical claims are less secure than in other candidates.
Excluding Vishny from the proposal is a significant attribution compromise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence reshaped understanding of labour demand, polarization, wage inequality and the local costs of trade. The work is empirically influential and policy-relevant.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure across both strands, with Hanson and Dorn as core coauthors on trade shocks. The task framework also draws on Acemoglu and Katz, so credit is partly shared outside this proposal.
assessment.maturity: Core papers date from 2003 to 2016, and the findings have been extended and in places qualified. Recognition of the labour-market effects of trade is likely to grow.
uncertainties: The task-approach credit is shared with Acemoglu, already a laureate, and Katz.
Some China-shock findings are debated on magnitude and persistence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Melitz model and Helpman's heterogeneous-firm trade theory changed how trade gains, selection and reallocation are understood, and became the workhorse of modern trade theory. The prize for new trade theory (Krugman) left this strand untouched.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central theoretical contribution, and Helpman is a leading architect of the broader trade and firm-heterogeneity agenda. Redding is a significant later contributor but the proposal stays at two.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of confirmation and extension. The quantitative-trade strand overlaps with other candidates such as B003 and B041.
uncertainties: The credit boundary with Bernard, Eaton and Kortum and the quantitative-trade literature is contested.
Competing claims within trade mean this strand may not be the one recognized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The sufficient-statistics approach and the elasticity of taxable income link tax theory to behavioural evidence and guide optimal tax and transfer design. The policy and empirical reach is large.
assessment.attribution: Saez is the main figure on optimal-tax formulas and taxable-income elasticities, with Slemrod an early empirical leader. Chetty and Stantcheva are important but more recent or broader, so credit is spread and Feldstein's early work cannot be recognized.
assessment.maturity: Core work is from the 1990s to 2010s and is still developing, with some elasticity estimates debated.
uncertainties: Credit across Feldstein's earlier contribution, Saez, Slemrod, Chetty and Stantcheva is diffuse.
Saez also appears on a separate inequality candidate, which could split support.
